title: POC: inference hosting strategy review - Cadence AI
next_steps: Redwood: send hosting decision matrix + cost model (Maya) by 2025-10-03
Redwood: run a 100 qps inference benchmark on dedicated SKU and share logs (Diego) by 2025-10-09
Cadence AI: provide representative prompt set + sample dataset for quality regression tests (Priya) by 2025-10-02
Schedule follow-up on security posture and network diagram (Samir + Diego) for week of 2025-10-06
action_items: Maya Chen: compile SLA examples and reserved capacity pricing; due 2025-10-03
Diego Alvarez: set up a short perf run (100 qps, 2k token avg) on Dedicated env and upload perf traces; due 2025-10-09
Priya Nambiar: share 300 prompt samples and the current token distribution histogram; due 2025-10-02
summary: Initial POC scoping between Redwood and Cadence AI to decide Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private for their conversational agent. Discussed workload profile, success criteria, target latency/cost SLOs, security constraints, and an initial benchmark plan. Agreed on data and timing for next steps.
topics: deployment mode tradeoffs: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private
transcript:
00:00 Maya Chen: Hi everyone, thanks for joining — I'm Maya from Redwood, AE for the Cadence AI account. Diego is our SE. Could you do quick intros?
00:12 Priya Nambiar: Hi, I'm Priya — lead ML engineer on the dialogue team. Evan's here, he's our CTO, and Samir is our security lead.
00:20 Evan Cole: Yep, thanks. We're looking to scope a POC to replace our existing inference path for the customer assistant.
00:28 Diego Alvarez: Great thanks. Quick agenda: confirm success criteria, go over workload profile and token counts, discuss Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private tradeoffs, and outline benchmarks + timeline.
00:42 Priya Nambiar: That works. To be upfront, our main asks are sub-200ms p95 for single-turn generation for short prompts and cost < $0.001 per inference on average — those are ballpark.
00:58 Samir Patel: Security constraints: we need SSO + SAML for admin, audit logs retention 12 months, and KMS integration for customer keys. On-prem is not impossible but we'd prefer VPC-first.
01:14 Maya Chen: Understood. Quick question on workload: what sustained QPS are you expecting during peak?
01:22 Priya Nambiar: Peak spikes at around 120 qps for the chat endpoint, sustained is more like 25-30 qps. Average tokens per request ~450 but that's skewed; median is closer to 180 tokens.
01:35 Diego Alvarez: Nice detail — that skew suggests we should model 95th+ tail token lengths in the benchmark. Also, prefix caching could help for repeat prompts.
01:48 Evan Cole: We currently have some in-house caching but it's brittle. Curious how Redwood's prefix/K V cache works — and is it compatible with our PII rules?
01:58 Diego Alvarez: We do prefix caching and KV cache for autoregressive models; cache configs can be tenant-isolated and you can opt out for sensitive flows. The cache can be encrypted at rest, and we can set TTLs per route.
02:12 Priya Nambiar: Okay, good. On model variants — we want to evaluate both a 70B open model and a 13B quantized option. Cost tiering is important: start small on hosted and move to dedicated if costs or latency require it.
02:29 Maya Chen: Common pattern. For the POC we often run a two-week hosted benchmark to validate quality and baseline latency, then a dedicated perf run if latency or cost gaps appear. For Private (VPC/on-prem) we usually reserve extra time for network validation and security acceptance.
02:45 Samir Patel: How long does the Private onboarding usually take? Our infra calendar is tight — lots of approvals.
02:52 Diego Alvarez: For VPC-hosted private with our control plane, typical timeline is 4-6 weeks for setup, longer if it's fully on-prem air-gapped. We can provide a checklist to accelerate.
03:05 Evan Cole: Ok that helps. Priya, what's our timeline?
03:09 Priya Nambiar: We'd like a 6-week POC and decision by mid-November. So ideally start early October.
03:15 Maya Chen: That's doable. We'll map milestones: deliver hosted baseline in week 1-2, dedicated perf run in week 3-4 if needed, security review and final decision week 5-6.
03:26 Diego Alvarez: For benchmarks, we propose: 1) throughput sweep up to 150 qps, 2) p50/p95/p99 latency for 5 representative prompt buckets, 3) cost per 1k tokens estimate across hosting modes, and 4) quality comparisons with your annotated prompt set.
03:43 Priya Nambiar: That aligns. One question on the dedicated SKU: what GPU types do you provision and can we pick quantization profiles?
03:51 Maya Chen: We offer configs with A100, RTX-class, and a later ML accelerator fleet — allocation depends on the reserved capacity tier. Quantization profiles are configurable; our Optimize team can recommend 8-bit/4-bit tradeoffs per model.
04:05 Samir Patel: For compliance, we need SOC2 attestation and an option to use our KMS for key wrapping. Also need network flows documented for our pen test team.
04:15 Maya Chen: We have SOC2 Type II and export a security package: SOC2 report, architecture diagram, and you can bring your KMS via customer-managed keys in Private or Dedicated. We'll attach the whitepaper after this call.
04:28 Evan Cole: About cost — Priya mentioned $0.001 per inference. Is that realistic if we include full token counts?
04:35 Diego Alvarez: Depends heavily on batching and tail behavior. With continuous batching and caching you can improve effective cost; dedicated reserved capacity tends to reduce per-token price for sustained throughput. We'll run your token hist and produce a cost model.
04:48 Priya Nambiar: We'll share token hist and 300 sample prompts. Note: about 8% of calls are multi-turn sessions with context up to 4k tokens. Those are our tail cases.
05:00 Diego Alvarez: Good to know. We'll include a long-context run in the benchmark.
05:08 Maya Chen: Any blockers from your side for hosted baseline?
05:11 Priya Nambiar: Only onboarding of our sample data and setting up SSO for the small test team. We also need to check data retention settings for logs.
05:21 Samir Patel: We prefer logs anonymized and to disable transcript storage where PII is present — can that be configured?
05:28 Diego Alvarez: Yes, route-level logging config can redact fields and you can opt out of long-term retention; we can set retention to 30 days for POC.
05:38 Evan Cole: What about failover — if hosted region has an outage, do we have an automatic fallback to Dedicated or another model?
05:46 Maya Chen: We support routing policies for region and capacity tier. For production, customers often combine Dedicated with a hosted fallback to preserve availability. For the POC we'll demonstrate fallback behavior in the dedicated perf run.
05:58 Priya Nambiar: For security review, Samir will need the network diagram and the control plane dataflow. Samir, any other ask?
06:05 Samir Patel: Also need RBAC examples, SAML SSO flow, and audit log sample records. Pen testing windows too.
06:12 Maya Chen: We'll include RBAC docs and a sample audit log extract.
06:16 Diego Alvarez: On the technical deep-dive side, we want to observe your p99 latency under synthetic traffic and then with your real prompt mix — that will guide kernel selection and batching params. We'll share the test harness and scripts.
06:29 Priya Nambiar: Great. A nit: sometimes transcripts show 'K V cache' as two letters in our logs and causes confusion in on-call; will there be consistent naming?
06:36 Diego Alvarez: We'll standardize naming in the artifacts.
06:39 Evan Cole: Anything else on decision criteria? To sum: latency SLOs, cost per inference, security posture, and operational runbook.
06:46 Maya Chen: That's it. For success criteria let's capture five bullets: 1) p95 latency < 200ms on median prompt set, 2) cost per inference target within 15% of your $0.001 goal, 3) no critical security blockers (SOC2 + KMS integration), 4) scalability to 150 qps with graceful degradation, 5) ops playbook for failover and monitoring.
07:09 Priya Nambiar: I like that.
07:12 Samir Patel: Agree but add enablement: runbook for incident response.
07:16 Maya Chen: Good call. We'll add runbook as #6.
07:20 Diego Alvarez: I'll outline the benchmark plan in the shared doc: perf scripts, sample size, metric definitions, and expected artifacts (flame graphs, pprof traces, request logs). We'll need access to your sample prompts and an API key for the hosted baseline.
07:36 Priya Nambiar: We'll provision a scoped API key.
07:40 Maya Chen: Next steps recap: Maya sends decision matrix + pricing and SOC2 package; Diego runs dedicated perf run if needed; Priya supplies prompt set and token histogram. We'll aim to kick off hosted baseline first week of October.
07:56 Evan Cole: Sounds good. Any concerns about data residency across regions? We need EU-only for some customers.
08:03 Diego Alvarez: We can pin region to EU for relevant routes and ensure data-at-rest stays within region for Dedicated/Private. For hosted multi-region we can route EU traffic to EU nodes.
08:15 Priya Nambiar: Okay, that addresses it. Thanks everyone.
08:19 Maya Chen: Thanks all — we'll follow up with the doc links.
08:23 Samir Patel: One last ask: include an NDA redline if needed — our legal might want it.
08:28 Maya Chen: Noted.
08:30 [end of recording]

Notes: transcript contains occasional transcription artifacts (e.g., 'K V' instead of 'KV', speaker label jitter). Shared artifacts mentioned: decision-matrix (link), SOC2-package (link), perf-scripts (link), onboarding-checklist (link).
